verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The half-power gain over (7.14) is present and is the same gain: the Lean conclusion carries exponent alpha + 1/2 where the hypothesis carries alpha. Where that half power comes from differs in form, not in content. The paper derives it from eps = 2^{-h l} together with the inequality on the reciprocal frequency stated just before Proposition 7.2 on p. 77; the Lean takes it as the explicit hypothesis hfrequency : BandBound s (1/2) (fun n => 1 / frequency n), i.e. the reciprocal frequency is itself of class eps^{1/2} times a growth power. The remaining differences are the class-encoding ones already described for eq-p077-3 and eq-7.14 (common growth degree, max 1 (delta x)⁻¹, abstract weight W for P(v), iteratedFDeriv for D^I). The S and delta degrees are the same existentially quantified p as in (7.14), consistent with the paper writing the same primed exponents in both displays.
